journal_lines: §aMud before anything else. §oSalt water and old wood and something alive in the silt.§o §lMangrove§l roots going everywhere.
§aStood in water to reach the trunk. The water was warmer than expected.
§aA frog on the root arch. Stepped around it. It did not step around me.
§aAerial roots hang like curtains. Cut through six before I found clear access to the trunk.
§aDense wood. §oSmells like salt and brine all the way to the heartwood.§o Heavy timber.
§aA heron on a snag nearby, watching. §oStill as a post, then gone between one blink and the next.§o
§aMud past the second knuckle for an hour. Worth it. Good §lMangrove§l take.
§aRoots tangled into other roots. Took the upper trunk, left the root mass alone.
§aThe water held the shape of where I stood for a moment after I moved.
§aTurtle on a low root, sunning hard. Worked the far side of the grove instead.
